parameter_notes.bays: number of structural bays along the block
parameter_notes.corridor_levels: the levels an internal street runs on
parameter_notes.cells: dwelling groups as [lowest level, highest level, index of the pierced level, tag]
parameter_notes.core_lines: the bays that become stair cores
parameter_notes.ends: bays beyond the last core, counted from the east end
parameter_notes.cb_merge: condenser storeys merged into the hall, as [lowest, highest]

V2_all_U_3levels.note: 9 levels, 3 streets, every cell a three-level U.

rules.name: AXIOM
rules.description: One node of type mass: the block as a single prism.

rules.name: R_LIFT
rules.description: mass becomes ground + mass, joined by 'supports' (access none). The ground plane becomes a node in its own right, which is what makes the pilotis legible to the graph at all.

rules.name: R_STACK
rules.description: mass becomes a chain of storey nodes on 'above' edges (access none).

rules.name: R_BAY
rules.description: A storey node is expanded into n bay nodes chained by 'party' edges whose access is NONE. The subdivision creates adjacency without access; every later rule has to supply the access explicitly.

rules.name: R_CORRIDOR
rules.description: On a street level each bay node splits into corridor + band. The corridor nodes form an open chain (access open) and each band gets exactly one 'door' edge. The internal street now exists as a path in the graph.

rules.name: R_LCELL / R_UCELL
rules.description: CONTRACT the run of band nodes of one bay into a single dwelling node. The door edge to the pierced level survives; the internal 'above' edges dissolve. The index of the pierced level decides the section: L, U, Gamma or Z. End units are the degenerate case: one level, entered from the stair lobby. This is the only production that reduces the node count.

rules.name: R_CORE
rules.description: A bay stack is relabelled as stairwells chained by 'stair' edges (access stair), with 'core_door' edges into the streets, the end units and the dwellings beside the core. Before this rule the graph has no vertical access at all.

rules.name: R_FACADE
rules.description: IDENTITY on the graph. The facade split (spandrel + ribbon) changes no node and no edge. It stays in the rule list as the honest record that shape and graph grammars are not in bijection: envelope is style, and the graph cannot see it.

rules.name: R_ROOF
rules.description: The bay nodes of the top level are relabelled as roof zone, and a terminal penthouse dwelling is attached to a core. A bay left anywhere below the top is an unresolved non-terminal.

rules.name: AXIOM
rules.description: A second axiom, plus ONE interface node standing for the block's corridor. Grammar GB sees nothing else of grammar GA, which is what lets the two be varied independently.

rules.name: R_STACK
rules.description: The same stacking production as GA2.

rules.name: R_MERGE
rules.description: CONTRACT adjacent storey nodes into one. The same graph operation as GA5 with the opposite programme: a collective room instead of a dwelling. The result is a node of high degree, which is the graph-theoretic definition of a social condenser.

rules.name: R_GALLERY
rules.description: A node joined to the hall by an 'open' edge: no wall, no door. The open edge is what distinguishes a gallery from a room.

rules.name: R_FACADE
rules.description: IDENTITY, as GA7. The curtain wall is the same facade rule with the split height at zero.

rules.name: R_CORE
rules.description: A core chain attached to the hall and the gallery by 'core_door' edges.

rules.name: R_BRIDGE
rules.description: The single production that joins the two grammars, through the interface node. In the composed graph BRIDGE is a cut vertex: remove it and the communal programme is stranded.
